catalog_quote: 2.1 Syllabic structure The vocabulary of Arem has monosyllables and sesqui-syllables. monosyllable: C V (C) sesqui-syllable: C-C V (C) A sesqui-syllable is composed of a main syllable C V (C) preceded by a pre-syllable C-. The main syllable is identical to a monosyllable. The pre-syllable is short and unstressed, without distinctive vowel, and its consonantal system is reduced. A pre-syllable can not exist alone. ... 2.2 Voice-type register system of Arem: - Arem has two sets of vowels: Series 1 with a high-clear register phonation; Series 2, with a low-breathy register phonation (indicated by the grave accent). ... - Syllables in voiced finals show a contrast between a modal tone and a glottalized tone: in series 1 /a~aˀ/, and in series 2 /à~àˀ/. tone_statements.citation: Ta, Tan. 2025. Arem: A Register Language without Tone. Proceedings of the Third International Conference on Tone and Intonation (TAI 2025), 129-133. doi:10.21437/TAI.2025-27.
tone_statements.quote: The results show that the Arem register is signaled by vowel quality and phonation type differences but not f0. However, the glottal codas in Arem are still intact, and their duration, f0, and phonation effects on the preceding rhyme are too variable across speakers and registers to consider Arem as a tone language. … Arem has a binary phonological contrast between high and low registers … The results of the second study (RQ2) refute the treatment of Arem as tonal [2, 28].
tone_statements.locator: Abstract (p.129), sec. 1.2 'Register contrast in Arem' (p.129) and sec. 4 'Discussion and Conclusion' (p.132)

tone_statements.quote: 4.3 Arem: Toneless Arem is reported to be toneless, but to have breathy phonation, and post-vocalic laryngeal constriction (Ferlus 1997, 2001). ... As we see above, Proto-Vietic is assumed to have contrasts in voice quality; modal vs. breathy, as Arem. Another laryngeal feature is the post-vocalic laryngeal constriction. This glottal constriction is what Diffloth (1989) called ‘creaky voice’. These two laryngeal configurations seem to be closely related to the origin of tones.
tone_statements.locator: p.179 sec. 4.3 'Arem: Toneless' and p.183 sec. 7
tone_statements.summary: No lexical tone; two-way voice register (modal/clear vs breathy) plus a glottalized ('constricted') vs plain contrast in sonorant-final rhymes; final -h retained as a segment (secondhand from Ferlus's data).

tone_statements.citation: Ferlus, Michel. 1999. Les disharmonies tonales en viet-muong et leurs implications historiques [Irregular tonal correspondences within Vietic and their historical implications]. Cahiers de Linguistique Asie Orientale 28(1): 83-99. doi:10.3406/clao.1999.1546 (open: Persée; HAL postprint halshs-01135816).
tone_statements.quote: Dans certaines langues vietiques minoritaires le système de base peut se réduire à 4 (+2) tons, soit parce que l’ancien -h final est préservé à la place des tons a⁵-a⁶ (mãliềng, arem, sách/rục, thavung), soit parce que certains tons attendus ne se sont pas régulièrement développés et se sont confondus avec les tons voisins (maleng brô, pong, toum, liha). Après -h final, dans les langues qui l’ont préservé, les tons notés a¹-a² sont les équivalents de a⁵-a⁶ par ailleurs. En maleng brô et en arem, pour plus de précision, le numéro du ton étymologique est rappelé entre des parenthèses bien que la notation utilisée rende cette indication superflue.
tone_statements.translation: In some minority Vietic languages the basic system may reduce to 4 (+2) tones, either because old final -h is preserved in place of tones a5-a6 (Mãliềng, Arem, Sách/Rục, Thavung), or because some expected tones did not develop regularly and merged with neighbouring tones (Maleng Brô, Pong, Toum, Liha). After final -h, in the languages that kept it, the tones written a1-a2 are the equivalents of a5-a6 elsewhere. In Maleng Brô and in Arem, for precision, the etymological tone number is recalled in parentheses although the notation used makes this indication superfluous.

tone_statements.summary: Per Ferlus's notation: Arem forms carry low-series grave accent vs unmarked high series, final -ˀ and -h; etymological tone categories 1-4, 7-8 recoverable from these, tones 5-6 replaced by -h.

sources.note: Ferlus derives VM tone systems from the relative chronology of (i) loss of final -ˀ/-h and (ii) devoicing of initials; languages that devoiced after -ˀ became a constriction/contour but while -h was still segmental got a 'four-tone basic system', and he explicitly puts Arem in that class with Maleng, Sách/Rục and Thavung (i.e. 2 registers x plain/glottalized, -h preserved). This is Ferlus's 'four tones' framing of Arem (contrast Honda 2005/Ta 2025 'toneless register language'); no phonetic description of the Arem tones is given.
